All in. Call my mighty bid at your peril. My cards are awful, and I need a hug.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I call your bluff.
Okay, Yivo showed us a good time. No one's denying that, but shklee hasn't offered our universe any kind of commitment, and we're 14 billion years old. That is too old to play the field.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I can't stand this!
Your lower horn!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'll just start you off with some bread. Some sexy, arousing bread!
This concept of "wuv" confuses and infuriates us!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Incoming torpedoes. Shields at maximum yarnell!
Guards! Seize him! Prepare to harvest the lower horn!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: OK, you can have my nose.
Silence! We will accept no more decoys. This is the McNeal.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Wait, I know her.

Attention, McNeal. We are reasonably satisfied with the events we have seen. Overall I would rate it a C+, OK, not great. As a result, we will not destroy your planet. But neither will we provide you with our recipe for immortality.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Way to overact,Zoidberg!
Attention, McNeal. Your unexpected marriage plan scares us. You stole our hearts as a single female lawyer, and so shall you remain -- or else!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: You see? TV audiences don't want anything original. They wanna see the same thing they've seen a thousand times before.
Pleased to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Actually, we've met once before.

Ladies and gentlemen, I'm proud to associate myself with a true hero. Mr. Fry, allow me to present you with the keys to the city. This one's for the deadbolt, this is for the top lock... I think this one's for the knob. The city's in a bad neighbourhood. Care to say a few words, son?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Uh... Heroes don't do drugs! Except for Drugman, I guess.
I beg to differ. Long have I waited for the one who played Spock. At last, we can begin.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Cool! A Star Trek convention!
I thank you, Fry. You know, you and I are of a kind. In a different reality I could have called you "friend".

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Episode 10, Balance of Terror.
Episodes 19, 46, 56 and 77.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Great list. Except, you forgot episode 66!
I meant me! Melllvar is the ultimate fan!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, I was confused because the scoreboard says something different.

Centuries ago, the videotaped adventures of the Enterprise crew rained down upon my planet. Over and over, I watched them. Especially the five with the energy beings. I am Melllvar! Seer of the tapes, knower of the episodes! Tremble before my encyclopaedic knowledge of Star Trek!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Tremble? I laugh. Nobody knows more about Star Trek than me!
Well, I guess I could move out of my parents' basement... maybe get a temp job.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Whoa, whoa! One step at a time.
My button has broken. The trivia contest has ended. I-I now have a surprise. You will perform a fan script, written by the ultimate Trek fan.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: You have my fan script?
Oh! I didn't realise Your Majesty was into that sort of thing!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: On second thought, I'll take that one.
Stick to the oath.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Right! I, Fry, who drank Bont the Viscous, who drank Ungo the Moist, who guzzled Zorn the Stagnant...
This is Your Majesty's harem. You may choose any of these maidens to be your royal consort.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Um, how about that one?
Fry must die so that Bont may live.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: What am I gonna do?
Only one. The absolutely flawless recitation from memory of the royal oath. By you.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Will there be cake?
Here you go, darlin'.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hey! I can breath and talk, just like a fish!
I'm sorry, my accent's atrocious. Hi, my name's Umbriel!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'm Fry. So, uh, am I gonna drown?
Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: And this is Dr. Zoidberg.
Oh, Fry, it is you!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I don't get it, Michelle. The last time I saw you, you were doing great. You had just dumped me and you were well on your way to getting you life back on track. Why'd you freeze yourself?
Fry? Is it really you?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I don't know. Is it really you?
It's not working out, Fry. I put your stuff out on the sidewalk!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I hate my life, I hate my life, I hate my life.
It's not that bad. Fate brought us together and now fate brought us here.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: No, you brought us here.
Everything is so different.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Not everything. There's still a roach problem.
Eurgh.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Nowadays, people aren't interested in art that's not tattooed on fat guys.
I just don't belong here. I don't know anyone, I can't find a vanishing cream that doesn't make me actually vanish. I don't even have a job.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, right. I was supposed to assign you a job. Let me just get your career chip installed. Hold out your palm. What are you scared of? It's just like getting your hand pierced.
No, I did it to get a fresh start. I didn't know what had happened to you -- no one did. The police were going to conduct a search but your parents felt it was a waste of taxpayer money.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: That's the same reason they kept me out of school. So, no one even cared that I was gone?
Oh, look! Some little kids.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: They'll save us. We're saved!
I love you. Don't you love me?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, sure. To the extent a man can love a woman. But this seems like a big step.
You know your problem, Fry? You're not ambitious. You should be chief.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: What do I need, ulcers?
What do you mean you don't know? Are you you or not?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Who wants to know?
It's not a "there". It's a "then". The future.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Whoa, whoa, girl. I thought you were talking about one of those motels where the bed is shaped like stuff.
Don't take this the wrong way, Fry, but your friends are a bunch of freaks.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Yeah, they're great, huh?
Every little thing reminds me of Enos.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Aw, I know how you feel. My grandfather died recently.
It's all so sad. At times like this, I just need someone to hold me. Mmm. You like holding me, don't you?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hey, you know what always cheers you up? Baking me a nice tray of sugar cookies!
How 'bout these cookies, sugar?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I shouldn't be here. I shouldn't even exist. But I do exist. Which proves... you can't really be my grandm--
Come back to bed, deary.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's impossible! I mean, if she's my grandmother, who's my grandfather?
I'm not worried about that.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Then you're a braver woman than I.
You remind me of Enos. Would you mind walking me home?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Uh, how far is it?
No! I give you...the Twitworm! Send.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Aaah! I'm sick of my head doing things! Leela!
Thank you, you repulsive disappointment.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Any word from Leela?
Previously, on Futurama.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Bender, I think you might be playing too much Dungeons & Dragons.
If I can't bring down Farnsworth, I can at least dumb down 'is Robot. Take 'im away and reset 'im to factory-stupid condition!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Bender, wait. While you can still calculate the future, just tell me What's gonna happen with me an' Leela?
Hello, shoppers. It's me, Mom!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hey who's the rocker jockey?
Pry out his fillings, feed him to the jackals and let's get on with the sale.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I don't think so. 'Cause, as vice chairman of the company, I gain voting control of his shares.
Don't be a fool, you idiot!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'll be whatever I wanna do! That Guy was the greatest businessman that ever lived. And before his mysterious death, he taught me everything he knew. But some things I had to learn myself. I learned that money is fine but in the end what counts is people... people you love. You can't put a price on that. So I'm giving up control of the company... to a man of enormous experience... Professor... Hubert Farnsworth.
By "monkey cake" I meant your ass!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, we've been skipping for hours. I need to pull over and take the wiz.
The new eyePhone is wonderful. I use it to check recipes and send threatening e-mails to unauthorized third party app developers.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Say, you're from one of those ethnicities that knows about technology. Why's it called an eyePhone?
I felt terrible when I heard about your money troubles and I thought maybe I could help out a sweet, young man by buying his anchovies.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Sorry. But the anchovies aren't for sale.
Don't let the door hit you on the way out, 'cause I don't want ass prints on my new door!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Uh, Ms. Johnson? Please bring in some more chair fuel.
Well, I've never seen my babies act this way. I blame today's violent media.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Violent media? What a load of--
Holy hell! You're going to eat them? Oh, well. Just make sure you eat them all, you're a growing boy. Toodle-oo! Dumb ass!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: What a nice lady!
Any button! They all retaliate!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Woo! Yeah! Hit him, hit him, hit him! Now this is the high life; watching apes mangle each other near celebrities.
What? Listen, you little bastard. I control the robot oil business and I won't let you ruin me. How much do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: You might as well put that chequebook away, because I've discovered something even more important My friends. And they aren't worth even a penny to me. That's why these anchovies are going on a pizza, so I can share the food I love with the people I like.
I call top bunk!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: My roommate's a monkey?
Well, you can always talk to me about anything, Fry. What's on your mind?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, it's... it's about my friend Bender.
I don't know what to say, other than "absolutely not". Your loss is a tragedy but our work--

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Aw, come on! You guys have forever to look for God. All I'm asking is one measly lifetime to find my friend.
Oh, how convenient! A theory about God that doesn't require looking through a telescope. Get back to work!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: That telescope is as much mine as anybody's. I'm using it whether you give me permission or not.
Let us out! We cooked our shoes in the dryer and ate them. Now we're bored.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hello? Has anyone out there seen Bender?
For $1, what tool is used to hammer a nail? Is it, A, a hammer? B, A nail? C...

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: B, nail, final answer!
Pathetic humans, prepare to write down the recipe!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hey, uh, what's with all the pots and pans? You building a wife?
Chitchat achieved! Are you ready to play?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I didn't come to play. I came to win. Now let's play.
Hello, little man. I will destroy you!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, even the news monster is acting strange. What are we gonna do?
Prepare for pleasantries. So Fry, what do you do for a living?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Me? Um, can I phone a friend?
What is our love's name?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Yivo. Yivo is the lover of all beings, male and female. But Yivo has no gender, thus Yivo has proclaimed that instead of "he" or "she," we are to use the word "shklee." And instead of "him" or "her," we are to use the word "shklim," or "shkler.
Then you should have filed a request 20 years ago.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'm sick of you and your bureaucracy!
Now listen, you filthy pig. No one can know about us. If anyone asks, I'll deny it.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Just like very other girl I've dated.
Lost something? I should have known you'd come here rather than follow proper procedure. And I did know. And that's why I came here.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Listen, Morgan, we're through. You're an evil, heartless woman and I never wanna see you again. However, would you help us get Bender back for old time's sake?
I sent the disk to be filed at the Central Bureaucracy. I did what I had to do, Fry; He was a bad robot.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: No, he was a bad friend. I want him back right now.
I-- I've never seen anything like this. Why is there yoghurt in this cap?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Uh, I can explain that. See, it used to be milk and, well, time makes fools of us all.
Oh, Fry!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Uh, wait, Bender's my roommate. He could be back any second.
You are all dismissed. Fry, I will speak to you alone.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Uh, wait, this is the other Fry's locker. I'm "Phry" with a P-H.
Admit it, Fry You're a slob. A dirty, filthy slob. Dirty boy! Dirty! Dirty! Dirty!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: What the hell's going on? I thought you were anti-dirty not pro-dirty.
I'm getting the doorbell. For me?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, uh, hello, sir. It's a lovely evening you have tonight. Um, I'm here to pick up your daughter.
Don't look at him!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: That was fun. Let's give him a treat!
You companion is a mutant?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: But if anyone asks, say she's an alien.
How charmingly unconventional.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I can eat a hotdog underwater.

On April 10, 2912, my late husband and I set off down Fifth Avenue aboard the Land Titanic, the largest street-going vessel ever built. Just four days into her maiden voyage, as we approached 32 Street, the line-liner struck a mailbox and went down. 2000 souls were lost that day, including my dear husband. In loving memory, I established the Mr. Astor Endowment, which this year supports the United Mutant Scholarship Fund.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Mutants? That's the kind of thing you are.
The gemerald ring that my husband was to give me in lieu of children. So what, I have a chandelier in my car made of those.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Not the gem. This passenger manifest. It turns out there were mutants on that ship, working below deck in the sewage galley.
Well! Rarely have I never!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Please, don't blame Leela. She's just a little ill-bred. You know how mutants are.
Say, would you Farnsworths care to be my guests tomorrow at the Astor Endowment Fundraiser? All the best families will be there.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: We can take 'em.
Call me Grandma like crazy! All the time!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Check it out, y'all. Everyone we invited is here.
It's the Y2K tryin' to lure us into an ambush. And I ain't buyin' it. Pass the baloney.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Are you two gonna be done soon?
What's happenin' up there? Did Kremlin Joe let fly with the nukes?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Not yet, commander. Yancy's just trying to steal my stuff as usual.
Well he'd better keep his hands off these bananas. Gonna need them when the radiation turns us all into monkeys.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: The Ronco Record Vault! Yancy'll never get his hands on you in here or my money back. Ah, The Breakfast Club soundtrack. Man, I can't wait till I'm old enough to feel ways about stuff. Stay safe, clover. I may need you again someday.
Ka-boom-boom.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hello? Madfellows? I need to- Okay, Leo Wong's about to destroy the violet dwarf. So, whatever I need to know to stop him, tell me now.
I said no way. This idiot don't look like he could handle those feministas.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I look like an idiot who can handle those feministas.
Sorry, no openings right now. What I need is security guard to keep nutcases out of my office.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'm good at keeping nutcases.
Fry, what you doing down there?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Just polishing your shoes, Mr. W.
Looking good, security. No feministas getting past you.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: No, sir. Not on my mustache's watch.
To hide your big, fat butt, that's why.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Now, sir, in fairness, Amy's butt is actually pretty hot.
Hmm. You and I think a lot alike. You really think you can stand up to those eco-freakos?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Sir, with me around, they'll be the least of your worries.
Can I be brutally honest, Fry? I always wanted a son.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: That hurt, but I can take it.
Looking for a job, eh?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Yes, sir. Nothing fancy. I'm willing to start at the bottom and infiltrate my way up.
He'll have to do better than that.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'll have to do better than that.
Give me your wallet or I'll cut you!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hey, Leela, get a picture of me being "mugged".
So, where are you taking my daughter tonight?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: A movie. A movie, ma'am.
My mother's nuts.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I beg you, Mrs. Astor, if you truly want to honor your husband's memory, treat these people with dignity, as he did.
Yes.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I had the Professor analyse the Alienese letter that was found with you.
I mutated from him!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Get outta here! What's Andy up to these days?
Did you know Andy Goldman?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Yeah, he was my neighbour. Why?
Bend it! Bend it! Bend it!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: What goes down, must back up!
Stop right there! I don't want to hurt you. I didn't want you to hurt me either!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Leela's going nuts and I can't save her unless I learn more about her mysterious past. Isn't there anything else you can tell me?
Don't sweat it, man.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'll never see Leela again.
She is not the boss of you! I am the boss of you!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Leela's gonna die. What would Delivery-Boy Man do?
Oh, let's just give it to him. Here.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: My nose! Light of my face!
Toys! Toys! Toys!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: And I can deliver them. Billions and billions in one night.
Now it's very nearly Xmas, And we've done the best we could,

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: These toys soldiers are poorly painted.
The machines are kinda tricky, Probably someone will be killed, But we gladly work for nothing--

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Which is good because we don't intend to pay.
So is our love.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Blech! We have to track down my nose before some alien snarfs it and does the worm. Who's in?
A woman! I'm scared.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, thanks to the Internet, I'm bored with sex. Is there a place on the web that panders to my lust for violence?
No! Don't ask about that! It-It would be, uh... boring!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Ah, forget it then.
Then why are you choking me right now?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Because I don't like being used.
I did not come back in time. My people lack that ability.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: But... I know you in the future. I-I cleaned your poop.
We had no choice. You were the only one who could help us. What is one life weighed against the entire universe?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: But it was my life.
The very same.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Can I also guess Mom?
Alas, our kitten-class attack ships were no match for their mighty chairs. The universe is doomed. Doomed!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Can I pull up my pants now?
The poop eradication is but one aspect of your importance.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: D-D-Did you just talk?
Well now it's your choice. Is there nothing in the future worth saving?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hm. Leela. But she doesn't think much of me.
Fry, do you remember some months ago when the Earth was attacked by flying brains?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Hmm. I remember the square-dancing stomachs. Although that might have been a Mylanta commercial. Wait! The brains! I do remember! But no one else does. They said I was crazy.
Uh, yes. Incidentally, I need to remain undercover so I'm blanking your memory.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Huh. Did everything just taste purple for a second? Oh, well. Let's go home, you dumb poop machine.
Being Brains, they feel compelled to know everything. And soon they will.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'm as mad as I've ever been.
Oh, we will. We will.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, I can't wait to tell everyone what happened.
We can explain!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: No, you can't. Shut your adorable trap!
Quite possible. We live long and are celebrated poopers. You will meet me when I'm a thousand years older.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Not if you don't freeze me.
Then outrun the blast on this Scooty-Puff Jr.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: OK, let's go through this once more--
We were afraid you would refuse.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Of course not. I love the future.
Verily. And that past nastification is what shields you from the brains. You are the last hope of the universe.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So I really am important? How I feel when I'm drunk is correct?

It all began 36 years ago... Now! On the planet Vergon 6. It was a veritable Eden, brimming with unique and irreplaceable species. Most of which were delicious. I was Supreme Fuzzler of a Nibblonian scientific outpost. It was paradise, until they came. One of your DOOP ships struck dark matter, little realizing it was not a natural deposit, but rather centuries of Nibblonian fecal material.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: The big faecal enchilada. Anyone else hungry?
But not on my terms. I will not be treated like... Hey, wait, aren't you amazed I can speak?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, actually, no. You forgot to blank our memories after you spoke last time.
Please. Our saviours foresee that in a thousand years, for one moment, the fate of the universe will depend on you. Since you will not live that long I must freeze you now.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, why couldn't you just ask me?
Then why did you let me eat Friskies and make bo-bo in a litter box?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, you're cuter that way.
For a thousand years, the evil Brains have been constructing the Infosphere, a giant memory bank twice the size of three ordinary memory banks.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: What's so evil about that?
Thank you for saving the universe, Fry. Here.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Whoa, thanks! If you ever need a saviour again, just ask.
You must choose The present or the future? To save yourself or to save Leela.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Yes! Here I come, future! Oh, no! Wait! I'm gonna get trapped in the Infosphere again! Just remember that Scooty-Puff Jr. sucks.
I don't understand.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Yes, you do! You came back in time to knock me into that freezer and now I came back in time to stop you.
You must not give up on her. I am stationed on a distant world known as Vergon 6. But, if you return to the future, I will transfer to Earth to give you what help I can.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: You really think I would have had a chance with Leela?
No. Perhaps you're thinking of my one man show about Vincent van Spock-- Uh, uh, I mean van Gogh! Damn!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Aha! You can't escape it!
Hey, a body! Buff, tan. Yeah, this is mine, alright!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Alright, you gas, what's the deal?
Truly, it was a paradise.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: And all you had to put up with was one really annoying Star Trek fan.
Oh, really, I've done too many things to remember one particular TV series. But if-if you want to discuss my books of poetry--

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Come on! Remember that episode where you got high on spores and smacked Kirk around?
Why did the world turn it's back on our obvious greatness?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: I'm literally angry with rage! Your co-stars may be gone but we can still get those episode tapes back for the whole world to see. Come on!
Welcome to the Head Museum. I'm Leonard Nimoy.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Spock? Hey! Hey... Do the thing!
I don't do that anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: This is unbelievable! What do you heads do all day?
Oh, you're right, I can't.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Uh, jeez, don't get upset. I mean, OK, I outwitted you, but--
I have absolutely no idea what you're talking about.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: You know. 1966? 79 episodes, about 30 good ones.
All in good time! I guess now is a good time. We're on Mars, in a forgotten cavern abandoned by the native Martians a million years ago.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Actually, it was five years ago. I remember 'cause they washed my socks.
In the violet dwarf star system.

Oh, cruel fate, I'm dead. They're putting me in my Sunday suit and shoving me in a wooden box. Now they're loading me into cold, cold ground. Hello! Here come the worms!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: If you were really dead, you wouldn't be laughing so hard.
Bite my shiny metal ass.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It doesn't look so shiny to me.
Hey, what happened to the TV?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It just went out.
Whoa, what an awful dream. Ones and zeros everywhere. And I thought I saw a two.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It was just a dream, Bender. There's no such thing as two.
Oh, it's true! I've been hiding it for so long.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's OK, Bender. I like cooking too.
Is it OK? I can't hear anything.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's an ale! Five gallons, six ounces!
Oh, sweet legal tender! Kid, tell the Donbot I'm quitting organised crime. From now on I'll stick to regular kind.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's funny, Bender; with you sick and Leela blind, only I know what really went on out there. Maybe someday I'll tell you the whole story.
This time, you'll have all the human comfort. We'll get a couple of toilets, some food cookers, maybe a puppy.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's good to be home.
Leela who?!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's good to see you. Is it good to see me?
There's a baby in there, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's just like riding a bicyc--
Let's see, where to start. OK, this is the TV area, that over there's the breakfast nook, and over here is where you'll be living which is great because, until now, it's just been wasted space.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's kinda cramped in here. I don't even have room to hang my clothes.
Who is that God-like figure?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's my brother, Yancy! And there, in his lapel, my seven-leaf clover! I knew he stole it.
It's the decaying ruins of Old New York. Welcome home, pal!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: It's my old neighbourhood. Man, this brings back a lot of memories.
I'm a thing.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Just leave me alone.
I've been married to worse.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Leela, I'm no doctor, but I'm afraid you be exhibiting symptoms of illin'. You're risking all our lives for your own personal obsession.
Wake up!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Leela, are you alright? You got wanged on the head.
And then Bender ran!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Leela, freak out later. We're not done escaping yet!
Phew!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Leela, we may not have much time left... so let's spend all of it reminiscing about Bender. He was like a big computer that ran on magic.
I'm too scared.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Leela, your scaredness is being transmitted straight to Bender. If you care about Nibbler, stop caring about him!
The planet's covered with 'em.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Let's bring back a couple of pocketfuls.
And I, I could be an acting coach!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Let's put on a show.
Yeah. Maybe it just learned to talk as a parlour trick, like Fry.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Like Fry! Like Fry!
Nope!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Listen, Leela, let me make it up by taking you out to dinner tonight.
I'm the greatest. Woo-hoo!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Look's like we got the old Bender back!
Fry" who?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Look, I know Flexo's your friend but I don't trust him alone with the atom.
You got the toenail! Oh!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Look, the food isn't what's important.
Well, that was dumb.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Looks like it's full of dig dogs.
Hey, check out the palm tree! It only gets sick when I cook brunch! How's that for a coincidence, Professor? With all your precious science!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, I don't wanna hurt Bender's feelings...
Ah!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, I wish we had a Robot to do stuff.
Nah, I'm comfy.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, Leela's been gone a long time. I hope she's at least making progress with Zapp Brannigan.
Whoa, slow down! This place just doesn't feel like home. It just isn't... cosy. Ah. I can barely move! It's perfect!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, it's a total sty! For the first time in a thousand years, I feel like I'm home.
Yeah, I'll do it when we get back.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, lucky for us Zapp Brannigan's nearby.
Come on, you call yourselves chumps?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Man, there's clouds of exhaust everywhere.
We'll be back after this word from Crazy Bender's Discount Stereo.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Married? Jenny can't get married.
Saved you.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Maybe Yivo was right. Maybe I should look for love closer to home. I don't know, Leela, you think maybe...
Here you go.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Mmm, let me get some of that suckling pig.
Yeah, when are you going to make a second Simpsons Movie? D'oh!

dialogue.text: Mr. Aragonés, I'm a big fan of your cartoons and your mustache.
Alright!

Neat!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: My God! He's become evil. I mean eviler!
Behold The Internet!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: My God! It's full of ads!
Psst, Fry. Take a dive.

dialogue.text: My fellow fish monsters, far be it for me to question your stupid civilisation or its dumb customs, but is squeezing each other's brains out with a giant nutcracker really going to solve anything? Dr. Zoidberg is my friend, and though a woman has come between us, I say we'll always remain friends. And you know why? One reason. You bastard! I'll kill you! You bastard!
Coma, coma, coma, coma, coma, chameleon!

dialogue.text: My soul mate is gone. Why should I go on living?
It's salt with water in it if that's what you mean.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: My vision's fading. I think I'm gonna die.
No friends.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: My whole world is gone. You can't possibly understand what it feels like to be so alone.
It's hopeless. We might as well turn in my head for the five cent deposit.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: No way! I'm not letting my best friend get recycled. Not for five cents, not for five hundred cents! Leela, I've got a plan!
Mind if I tag along? I gotta bring my ass in for servicing. The recall notice says it could burst into flames in a low-speed collision.

dialogue.text: No wonder you've been staying at the back of conga lines lately.
Yuck! That's the least appetising calzone I've ever seen!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: No! That's my dog in there. It's an outrage, I say! I'm taking him home and I'd like to see anyone try and stop me. Uh-oh!
Everyone we ever knew? Nah, I never liked those guys.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: No! They did it! They blew it up! And then the apes blew up their society too. How could this happen? And then the birds took over and ruined their society. And then the cows. And then... I don't know, is that a slug, maybe? Noooo!
Yep!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: No, Professor, don't give up. There were plenty of times in my century when I was gonna give up but I never did. Never! Hey, are you even listening to me? Oh, I give up!

dialogue.text: No, really, I don't-- Mmm!
Who should be unfreeze next?

dialogue.text: No. No! Oh, my God! It's Pauly Shore!
Who put this in here?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Nooo! Are you people satisfied? This gentle visitor is dying! And we'll never even know why he came.
What's happening? Just in time!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Nooo! I could fit if I didn't have these damn arms!
That's impossible!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Now, if you'll excuse me, I'm working on Seymour's doghouse.
My chair's too hard. It's a real pain in the, uh, whattya call it? Lower back! Yeah, that whole region.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: OK, I gotta break down that gate, beat up those three guards, steal that chopper and rescue Bender.
Idiot.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: OK, OK, never mind. I'll just ask those people for directions.
Oh, I think I'm gonna output.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: OK, you stay in bed. I'll eat yours.
You seem a tad wound up, buddy. And your face is greasy. Real greasy! You been up all night?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Of course I've been up all night! Not because of caffeine. It was insomnia. I couldn't stop thinking about coffee. I need a nap. Coffee time!
Like putting too much air in a balloon!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Of course! It's so simple!
Wake up and feel the coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh no! I'm late for work again!
Yabba dabba doo.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh uh, I'm late for dinner with Leela.
Alright, a tie! I win again!!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, I'm a scuzzball.
Wait! There's someone you know!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, can't you leave me alone? I'm miserable enough already.
Well, you meet half the qualifications.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, good, a physical! Once they examine my fragile, naked, pink body, they'll see I'm not a--
Yep. That's exactly the lie we used to get past your guards.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, great space king, I humbly beg you to return my human horn.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, hey, Leela, uh, can I talk to you for a minute? In private?
Watch it!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, it's just that I love Leela something awful. Do you think a space-age dame like her would ever marry a two-bit, low-life delivery boy like me an' also I 'ave bad posture and severe financial problems?
Activating ice drill.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, my God! It's out of ice! Like some outer space Motel 6!
Froggy went a-courtin' and he did ride, uh-huh, uh-huh Well, Froggy went a-courtin' and he did ride, Blah, blah, blah, something, Bender is great! Froggy went a-courtin' and Bender is great, uh-huh--

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, my God! They dug up a bag of olestra chips from my time! There must be layers and layers of old stuff down there.
Uh, wait, old... spice. Let me have a go at this mechanised chap. I can be quite the rough customer.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, no! Poor Bender.
Well, OK. But I don't want people thinking we're robo-sexuals. So, if anyone asks, you're my debugger.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, no, it's the Cyclops! Don't look! Don't look!
How should I know? And how come you never ask if I'm okay? I'm feelin' a little neglected here!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, sorry. Are you okay, Bender?
The eyePhone records everything. All I did was add a laugh track and twit it to my 10,000 followers.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, that reminds me. It's time to twit my hourly twupdate. 'Sup, followers? Fry here. Burpin' eggs. Scratchin' my underarm fungus. Lookin' for love. Send.
Say, why'd you get me a subscription to the Daily Growl? That's not a reputable journal of opinion.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, that's also for Seymour. I'm getting everything ready for when he's cloned.
Yes. But first, since I love you all so much, I'd like to give everyone hugs. Come here, Fry!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, uh, but I don't want to.
An upgrade? But I thought we all agreed I was perfect! Fry, didn't we agree I was perfect?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah, no, you're pretty perfect.
No. It's inhabited by robots!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh. Kinda like how a warehouse is inhabited by boxes.
And now, a man who needs no introduction. Fry, get up there!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Oh. Thank you. Y'know, when I was first asked to make a film about my nephew, Professor Farnsworth, I thought "Why should I?" Then later Leela made the film. But if I had made the film, you could bet there would have been a lot more topless women on motorcycles! Roll film!
Stop tempting me! For once in my life I have inner peace.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Pfft! That's for losers. C'mon, sin your heart out.
And even though the computer was off and unplugged, an image stayed on the screen. It was... the Windows logo!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Pft, that's not scary!
OK, Fry, grab a Kleenex for this one, 'cause there's no God and your idiotic human ideals are laughable!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Phew! That's a load off my mind.
Get her purse!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Please let us live! We'll put out milk and cookies for you!
Randy?! 'Ave you been hangin' out with Randy?!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Please, Bender. If everything is a chess game for you, you must know how to help me.
No further answers, Your Honor.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Please, Justice Dogg, Leela and her friends are completely innocent.
Haven't I done enough already?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Please... Stop the monster. Just do that one thing.
Well, the bottom's all stocked with cheap stuff. Who's in the mood to party? Whoo!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Poor, Leela. I feel like I ruined her life.
This has been a test of the Emergency Hypnotoad System. Had this been an actual hypnosis, you would go limp and watch whatever crap comes on next. Comin' up next Futurama!

dialogue.text: Professor, my Fry-fro's all frizzy.
I go not by the name of Bender, you fleshy fool. I am Titanius Anglesmith, fancy man of Cornwood.

dialogue.text: Professor, something's bothering me.
But we still have one hope, my big televised debate! I'm our A in the hole!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Professor, who's debating for your side?
No, it's Fry who's crazy in this one.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Psht, I'm not crazy.
Hey, Fry, check out my laser-guided fishing rod.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Quiet, Bender, you're scaring away the fish.
We could have another one, if it would make you guys feel better.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Really? No, that's not necessary.
Yeah, but the rents are outrageous. Why don't you just come move in with me?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Really? That'd be great! You sure I won't be imposing?
I don't need to drink, I can quit anytime I want! So they made you a delivery boy, huh? Man, that's as bad as my job.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Really? What do you do, Bender?
No, I'm whacked out on life. My friends, I found religion.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Religion? Is this another scam to get free yarmulkes?
You're better off dead, I'm telling you, dude.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Santa Claus is gunning you down!
Well, he wasn't in the, uh, kitchen room.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Say, Bender, can I hold that map for a second?
Shut your fat mouth!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: See you guys Monday!
Yeah! What are you chicken?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Shut up, you two! We can kill ourselves when we get home!
My what, now?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Since when is the internet about robbing people of their privacy?
What part of "nay" doesn't thou understand?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Sir, I'm outfitting an expedition to a monastery high in the Himalayas. I'll need a long-sleeved coat.
You can trust anything.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So now Leela's all crotchety because she thinks I'm not attracted to her in the Professor's body.
Well, let's get looting!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So this thing's gonna destroy the whole city? What the heck is it?
The very idea!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So we set up this little charade based on an episode of Speed Buggy.
Nice catch, idiot!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So where are we going anyway?
Get it off! Get it off! Get it-- Uh-oh! How many roads must a man walk down, before you-- Keep those things off of me! Magnets screw up my inhibition unit!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So you flip out and start acting like some crazy folk singer?
Oh, and bring my toboggan.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So, Leela, were you able to help the penguins?
Come to Daddy, sweetie-ookums.

We're both expressible as the sum of two cubes.

dialogue.text: So, uh, Flexo. Sorry about crushing your body like that. You OK now?
It's used to it!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So, uh, how are you two snooky-poopums doing?
Yeah. Would you kindly shut your noise hole?

dialogue.text: So, who's that weird-looking guy?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: So? What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Speaking of which, try these nachos.
Oh, yeah! That calms the shakes. Hey! Aw, quit it! Come on!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Stop! The robot's not your enemy! He's just a poor, misunderstood--
Enough of this crap! I'm catching the next pimpmobile outta here! But before I go I have one thing to say. Bite my shiny metal--

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Stop! You can't say the next word.
Oh no, you didn't.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Stop. Somewhere, some time, Leela's waiting for me. We need to keep looking for a backwards time machine.
That'll teach those other horses to take drugs!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: That's it! You can only take my money for so long before you take it all, and I say enough. I've got one dollar left, and this one I'm holding on to! Oh, no you don't! I may not know much about horses but I know a lot about doing anything for one dollar! If you think bad luck can defeat me then you don't know my name is Philip J.--
Huh? Wasn't me. Must be some of that urine your all so proud of.

dialogue.text: That's not urine, it's oil.
Hey, Fry, I'm steering with my ass!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: That's the best thing I ever saw!
OK, I've constructed an elaborate lie I'll call Angle-ine while pretending to be Flexo, arrange a date, show up disguised as him and catch her two-timing me with myself.

dialogue.text: That's thinkin' like a man.
Well, I'm sick of her.

dialogue.text: The ship? But you just started dating.
I'm so lonely. I'm gonna go eat a bucket of ice cream. A bucket of--

dialogue.text: The spoon's in the foot powder.
Check.

I mean a good calculator. Minus the food, the bunny rabbit wallpaper-- I'm getting 100 bucks a kid and they're costing me 110!

dialogue.text: There goes my new kitchen cabinets.
Yeah, yeah, amen. Listen, I'm one of those lazy homeless bums I've been hearing about. Could you point me to the free booze. Oh, yeah! Oh, yeah!

dialogue.text: There's this girl who I really like but she thinks I'm a jerk. Can you help me?
It's a phone call, dingus.

dialogue.text: These eyePhones are phones, too?
Fry, what's wrong?

They're strapping her to juicer. Oh, they're putting some ice cubes in the glass under it.

dialogue.text: This can't be happening.

dialogue.text: This is Fry. If you're calling about the used towels for sale, they're still available for $45 each.
Alright!

dialogue.text: This is great! I haven't had time off since I was 21 through 24.
What a waste.

dialogue.text: This is it. My Ronco Record Vault. I still remember the combination Three. It's stuck!
Keep 'em to yourself, Pops!

dialogue.text: This is where I brought my girlfriend on our very first date.
And why is the Slurm pouring into this sewer?

dialogue.text: This isn't Slurm at all!
That's basically what I do every day.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: To the end of the universe.
To the flying machine!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: To the left! No, to the up! U-turn! U-turn!
Whatchoo talkin' 'bout, Fry?

Xmas dinner, everyone.

We're in here too.

dialogue.text: Uh, it's probably better if we don't know. Uh, mystery of life and whatnot.

dialogue.text: Uh, preparing for takeoff.

dialogue.text: Um, OK. Let's go bowling.

dialogue.text: Wait a second. You're a bender, right? We can get out of here if you just bend the bars.
See? Nothing. Told you, losers.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Wait! There on the screen. It's that guy you are.
Well, I'm off.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Wait! We could hide you. We'll pile fruit on you and claim you're a bowl.
You should say someth'n' else.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Wait. I know where we can get beeswax. From those giant space bees that nearly killed us, and we swore we'd never go back there.
Yes, I do. That's how I'm built.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Way to bend it!
Ah, this thing stinks.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: We checked 90,000 cans of Slurm and all we won was this junk. I never wanna see another can of Slurm again. Man, am I thirsty.
Guys, you'll never believe what happened. First I was God, then I met God!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: We climbed a mountain and locked up some monks.
What?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: We don't need it anymore. Yivo proposed. We're moving in with shkler.
A surprise funeral? For me?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: We just wanted to show you that you really will be remembered.
I'm back, baby!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: We made it! We're alive!
Of course! Bender is a lone wolf. A solitary eagle. A cuddly baby tapir! And that's why I love him!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, I guess we'd better clean up these millions of hearts.
With what?

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, I went to another universe, and I fell in love with a giant octopus, and now I'm pope of a new religion.
Hey, there's my little space heater.

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, I'm moving out!
If it's any consolation, my life is great! Babes! Bucks! I got it all!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
dialogue.text: Well, at least I learned Leela's a lost cause. I give up.
Stay away from our women! You got metal fever, boy! Metal fever!

dialogue.speaker: Fry
